claims.statement: Freeman centrality paper was published in Social Networks 1(3) 1978-1979 pp215-239
Freeman reports earlier Bavelas 1948, Leavitt 1949/1951 and inconsistent small group communication results accumulated in 1950s-60s
Freeman distinguishes three intuitions degree, closeness, betweenness for point centrality and separates absolute, relative and graph-level measures
Graph centralization normalized sum of differences to maximum among graphs of same order
For undirected simple graphs n>=3, degree centralization uses sum(kmax-ki)/((n-1)(n-2))
Five-node star degree vector 4,1,1,1,1 gives centralization 1; five-node cycle all degree2 gives 0
Five-node path degree 1,2,2,2,1 gives centralization 1/6; star and path both 4 edges
Degree, closeness and betweenness reflect different properties, not necessarily actual leadership, causal influence or value
Disconnected, directed and weighted graph settings require separate conventions and cannot re-use simple undirected formulas without adjustment
